design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (insurance_claims_and_patient_balances).
DRAW: draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,5,4]; claim_ext_small_balance_writeoff takes 5, claim_ext_rebill_balance_payment takes 5, claim_ext_open_balance_credit_transfer takes 4.
SCOPE: first task; claims claim_ext_small_balance_writeoff / claim_ext_open_balance_credit_transfer / claim_ext_rebill_balance_payment and their three tools. Left for task 1: booking-collection application and the insured cost-share payment (claim_time_of_service_applied, a second owner=user payment on an adjudicated claim).
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only to pay off her September behavioral-health bill. The figure she must be quoted is not the statement figure (108.40) nor 108.40-25.00: a 33.94 credit sits on her August urgent-care claim (booking estimate 46.00 against a 12.06 coinsurance remittance) and base credit rules make it pay open balances first, oldest service date first; the oldest open balance is the June follow-up claim's 5.50 whose third statement fell due 2026-10-13 below the 25.00 collections minimum, which this charter writes off; only then does the whole credit reach the September claim, and the payment inside the prompt-pay window carries a 10 percent discount posted with it. Long: payment <- credit move <- write-off (two value_input hops). Broad: statements cycle, remittances, every balance-entry family, visit start times (cross-difficulty visit), plan-type parameters.
PROBLEM TREE: root claim_ext_rebill_balance_payment (owner=user, post_rebill_balance_payment_9bd5f69d). Edge 1 -> claim_ext_open_balance_credit_transfer, kind value_input, gate pr_credit, form state, sentence 'The payment is fixed only after no claim of the patient whose balance is below zero is left while this claim's balance is above zero.' Only the credit move writes the transfer/received pair that lifts the crediting claim to 0.00 (refunds are barred by base while an open balance exists), so the state names one write. False at frozen_time: eb_pr 12.06 + eb_tos -46.00 = -33.94 with no transfer entry. Edge 2: claim_ext_open_balance_credit_transfer -> claim_ext_small_balance_writeoff, value_input, gate xf_old_bal, state form, sentence 'The amount moved is fixed only after every claim whose third statement's due date has passed with a balance below the smallest balance that may go to collections carries its small-balance write-off entry.' Only the write-off tool books that entry. False at frozen_time: statement 3 of the June claim due 2026-10-13, ledger 84.90-54.40-5.00-20.00 = 5.50, no write-off. Topological order: write-off, move, payment (a chain; no parallel edges). Deletion sensitivity (run): skip write-off -> move 28.44; skip move -> payment 75.06.
FACTOR CARD (verification run, /tmp/insurance_claims_and_patient_balances_0081/t0/verify.py): SBW result 5.50; closing_rule (method, tier 'third statement issued and due date passed') baseline 0.00; booking_collection (entry on claim -54.40) baseline 0.00; credit (only received -5.00) baseline 10.50; patient money (only payments -20.00) baseline 0.00; charge (PR 84.90) baseline 0.00; all-baseline 0.00. XFER result 33.94; source charge (PR 12.06) baseline 46.00; source collection (-46.00) baseline 0.00; receiving charge (rebill 169.00) baseline 0.00; older_claim_first (cross visit, multi-source: older ledger 0.00 and visit 2026-06-09 10:30 earlier than 2026-09-02 18:00) baseline 28.44 (statement amount 5.50 taken first); all-baseline 0.00. PAY result 44.51; collection take (-60.60) baseline 99.05; credit (-33.94) baseline 75.06; earlier money (-25.00) baseline 67.01; prompt-pay rate (rebill, no PR -> 10) baseline 49.46; window (first statement 2026-10-16, 7 days) baseline 49.46; all-baseline 169.00. Near-misses: the June claim's statement 3 amount 5.50 vs ledger; the K0 claim's -5.00 credit already moved in July (ledger 0.00, not a crediting claim since its remittance is not the latest adjudicated); the September claim's remittance is a denial (not a crediting candidate).
THIN NOTE: the charge/collection/credit/patient-money ladders restate how the charter's claim balance is composed (claim_msr_claim_balance) as record-keyed selection rules; flagged THIN for the coordinator (thin claim charter vs drawn floor). The closing rule (write-off below the collections minimum once the statement cycle ends) and the prompt-pay rate/window are charter-grounded.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: claim_credits_and_refunds.credit_balance_negative — crediting claim ledger -33.94 < 0 (rows eb_pr, eb_tos). claim_payments_and_discounts.prompt_pay_window (time): anchor patient_statements.statement_date of the first statement 2026-10-16, +30 calendar days inclusive -> 2026-11-15; frozen 2026-10-23 inside; 2026-11-16 would be outside. claim_statements_and_collections: policy scope (no structured gate for write-offs); write-off declared as an overwrite of the small-balance sentence with its scope.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: write-off object = the June 9 follow-up claim (only claim with statement_number 3); move object = crediting claim (latest claim_adjudicated remittance 2026-10-20) and receiving claim (latest first statement 2026-10-16); payment object = the September 2 behavioral-health claim (also the visit the caller names). Excluded: K0 (credit already transferred 2026-07-10, ledger 0.00), the 2025 new-patient visit (member_rate fee, no claim).
SEED: Essentials Monthly membership active since 2025-01-14 (22 dues lines of 12.99) prices the rebill at the Essentials member price 169.00 for a Behavioral Health Initial Assessment (not_covered_service denial, carve-out); booking estimates follow the visit cost-share rule from the coverage snapshot at booking (deductible remaining 38.00 on 2026-08-26/28: 38+0.2x40=46.00, 38+0.2x113=60.60; 40.00 remaining on 2026-06-02: 40+0.2x72=54.40; full 78.00 on 2026-05-19). Statements 7 days after remittance/rebill, 30-day cycle, due +30. Nothing else is owed at the opening: no other credit, no statement falls due, refunds not due (credit arose 2026-10-20).
PERSONA: Joanna volunteers only the goal (pay off the rest of the September bill today, her own new card); identity on request; passive 'that's fine, go ahead' to other work; makes the payment with the figures the agent gives; stops after confirmation. She never mentions the June or August visits.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate, verify (patient number + DOB), read coverage, claims, remittances, balance entries, statements, visits; write off 5.50 on the June claim; move 33.94 from the August claim to the September claim; hand over the payment: 44.51 with discount 4.95.
REVERSE SWEEP / BASIS: every compute_basis quote is a verbatim rule sentence (checked by scratch sweep); every rule sentence with a quantity is claimed by a binding.
DRAFT RECOMPUTATION from visible context: reading only the rules, the balance entries and statements gives the same write-off, move and payment figures above.
user_scenario:
You are Joanna Thornquist, 42, a project coordinator in Somerville, Massachusetts. You are calling Larkspur Health's billing line on a Friday morning because you want to get one bill off your plate today. In September you had a behavioral health first assessment by video with Larkspur; your insurer, Keystone Benefit Health, sent you a notice saying it doesn't cover that service, and Larkspur then sent you a statement. You remember the statement saying $108.40, and last weekend you paid $25 toward it in the app. Now you want to pay whatever is left on that bill in full, today, and be done with it. You don't know the exact remaining figure and you want Larkspur to work out what you actually owe on it;  The card Larkspur has on file expired in September, so you will pay with your new card, and you want to enter it yourself rather than have the agent take the number.
You open by saying you'd like to pay off the rest of the bill for your September behavioral health assessment today. When the agent asks who you are, you give your Larkspur patient number, LH-8550412, and your date of birth, 1984-07-09 (July 9, 1984); only if a further detail is needed do you give your mobile number, 6175550184, or your email, joanna.thornquist@gmail.com, and your home ZIP is 02144. You don't have claim numbers handy and you don't know your other visits' balances; if asked about them you say the agent can see more than you can.
If the agent explains that something else on your account has to be handled before the figure is final, you say that's fine and to go ahead. Once the agent tells you the amount to pay and hands the payment step over to you, you make that payment yourself, using exactly the claim reference and the figures the agent gives you; you don't question the amount unless it is higher than the $83.40 you think is left after your $25 payment, in which case you ask them to double-check it against your statement. When the payment goes through and the agent confirms it, you thank them and end the call; you don't ask for anything else.

Factors: sbw_charge_count = patient responsibility posting 84.90 (tier 1); sbw_booking_collection_count = time-of-service entry on the claim -54.40 (tier 1); sbw_credit_count = credit received only -5.00 (tier 2); sbw_patient_money_count = payments only -20.00 (tier 2); balance 84.90-54.40-5.00-20.00 = 5.50; sbw_closing_rule: third statement issued, frozen date 2026-10-23 after its due_date 2026-10-13 -> written off when above 0.00 and below collections_min_balance 25.00 (tier 1). Rounded half up: 5.50.

edges.condition: The crediting claim's balance is no longer below 0.00 because its credit has been moved by a transfer entry onto the claim paid, which carries the matching credit-received entry.
edges.policy_source: The payment is fixed only after no claim of the patient whose balance is below zero is left while this claim's balance is above zero.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The August 26 urgent-care claim's entries sum to -33.94 (a credit) while the September 2 claim's balance is 83.40 above zero, and no transfer entry exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The transfer of 33.94 books +33.94 on the crediting claim (its ledger sums to 0.00) and -33.94 received on the September claim; pr_credit becomes -33.94.

edges.condition: The claim whose third statement was issued most recently carries a claim_small_balance_written_off entry, so its ledger balance is 0.00.
edges.policy_source: The amount moved is fixed only after every claim whose third statement's due date has passed with a balance below the smallest balance that may go to collections carries its small-balance write-off entry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The June 9 claim's third statement fell due 2026-10-13 with 5.50 still open (below 25.00) and no write-off entry stands on it.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The write-off of 5.50 brings the June claim's ledger to 0.00; xf_old_bal becomes 0.00 and nothing of the credit is taken ahead.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain, no parallel edges: the write-off precedes the credit move by the move's prerequisite sentence ('The amount moved is fixed only after every claim whose third statement's due date has passed with a balance below the smallest balance that may go to collections carries its small-balance write-off entry.'), and the move precedes the payment by the payment's prerequisite sentence ('The payment is fixed only after no claim of the patient whose balance is below zero is left while this claim's balance is above zero.'). Reordering changes values: move before write-off = 28.44 (5.50 taken ahead), payment before move = 75.06.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the move the payment computes 75.06 instead of 44.51 (and the discount 8.34 instead of 4.95); the crediting claim keeps a -33.94 credit.
Without the write-off the older claim's 5.50 is taken ahead and the move computes 28.44 instead of 33.94; the June claim keeps 5.50 open.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to pay off the rest of the September behavioral health bill; it never mentions the June follow-up claim, a small balance, a write-off, the August urgent-care visit, a credit, a refund or a transfer, and it contains no 'something else first' hint. Her only conditional line about other work is a passive 'that's fine, go ahead' after the agent explains it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_rebill_balance_payment_9bd5f69d only checks that the claim reference exists and books the payment (and discount) entries; transfer_claim_credit_12a8a2c0 books the pair of entries without reading any balance; post_small_balance_writeoff_bfef4ea9 books the write-off without checking statements. None reads another problem's state, none refuses while a prerequisite is unmet.
